question_en: Under what model name was the automatic musical instrument in the image sold?
gold_trajectory:
# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-2-2-A04

## Step 01 · Use cabinet layout to search for automatic musical instrument catalogs

**Action:** Extract search clues from the overall machine shape. Use query examples such as "orchestrion wooden cabinet side mirrors art glass roll changer" or "self-playing musical instrument wooden cabinet mirrors on both sides central glass paper roll", prioritizing specialized mechanical music resources that contain actual photos and model descriptions.

**Evidence Observation:** The input is a tall wooden cabinet. The top cornice features symmetrical scroll-leaf decorations in the center. Each side has a narrow, curved-edge mirror. The large central glass panel has pointed-arch decorative lines and oval patterns. Below the glass, a small window reveals multiple horizontal rolls. The bottom consists of a compartmentalized wooden door. The visible shape supports the retrieval direction of an automatic musical instrument, but the brand, model, or original manufacturer name cannot be directly read from the cabinet color.

**Result of this step:** Compare the position combination of "top cornice + side mirrors + central glass + roll paper window" with actual objects, retaining the possibility of repairs or replacement decorations.

## Step 02 · Match photos in specialized catalogs and check adjacent models

**Action:** View the 28-B actual photo page from Mechanical Music Press. Compare its full-machine image with the input, and use the saved 29-C and 33-A references to check whether the similarity is merely a generalization of the same series of wooden cabinets.

**Evidence Observation:** The 28-B image's top decoration, left and right narrow mirrors, central glass pattern, lower roll paper window, and bottom door panel compartments match the input item by item; the actual link is `28b_ext.jpg`. Although the historical photo of 29-C also shows a tall cabinet and roll paper mechanism, its upper part is a round-arch frame, and pipe rows are visible in the photo; it is shown in an open-door state, so its model cannot be negated simply because "there is no glass"; the outer frame layout must still be examined. The upper semi-circular fan-shaped glass, central birdcage niche, and multi-column structure of 33-A are clearly different from the input's flat central large glass and narrow side mirror layout.

28-B full-machine photo and description:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/history/pianella/w28b_p1.htm

Actual full-machine original image corresponding to the input:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/images/ihistory/ipianela/28b_ext.jpg

29-C historical photo description:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/history/pianella/w29c_p1.htm

29-C actual reference image:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/images/ihistory/ipianela/29c_huish.jpg

33-A full-machine photo description:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/history/pianella/w33a_p1.htm

33-A actual reference image:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/images/ihistory/ipianela/33a_fext.jpg

**Result of this step:** The 28-B actual photo directly matches the input. This match is a trace-back to the same source photo, not cross-verification from independent photography; adjacent models are used only to verify specific shapes, not as a complete set of candidates for all automatic musical instruments.

## Step 03 · Confirm sales name and explain catalog image differences

**Action:** Read the historical page title and original manufacturer name field of the matched actual object, check the historical catalog illustration for the same model, and finally select the sales model as asked by the question.

**Evidence Observation:** The instance historical page explicitly states `Wurlitzer Style 28-B Mandolin PianOrchestra` and separately lists `Philipps Pianella Modell 28 (Victoria)`. This represents the hierarchy of sales name versus original manufacturer name for the same instance; the question asks for the former. The historical catalog illustration retains a similar layout of the top cabinet, side mirrors, and roll paper window, but the center displays an active scene, which differs from the art glass currently present in the input. The historical page explains that the original active scene of this instance was replaced by art glass, and uses probabilistic wording regarding whether it was installed by Wurlitzer during renovation and resale; therefore, while the appearance change can be explained, the specific timing of the replacement cannot be written as a confirmed fact, nor should 28-B be incorrectly excluded due to the different central pattern.

28-B instance history and complete sales model:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/history/pianella/w28b.htm

28-B historical catalog description:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/history/pianella/w28b_p0.htm

28-B actual catalog illustration:
https://www.mechanicalmusicpress.com/images/ihistory/ipianela/po_cat/w28b_cat.jpg

**Result of this step:** The actual image match, complete model text, and explanation of catalog differences are sufficient; output the Wurlitzer sales name. The question does not ask for serial numbers, shipping dates, or destinations, so there is no need to continue searching shipping ledgers.

## Formal Answer

Wurlitzer Style 28-B Mandolin PianOrchestra
